subject: biology
title: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
key_idea: Animal and plant cells are **eukaryotic**: their DNA is enclosed in a nucleus. Bacterial cells are **prokaryotic**: they are much smaller and their DNA is not in a nucleus. Each structure inside a cell has a job, and cells are measured in micrometres.

blocks.text: Every living thing is made of cells. There are two types. **Eukaryotic cells** are the cells of animals, plants and fungi. They have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and genetic material enclosed in a **nucleus**.

**Prokaryotic cells** are bacterial cells. They are much smaller than eukaryotic cells. They have cytoplasm and a cell membrane, surrounded by a **cell wall**. Their genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus.

A prokaryotic cell has one loop of DNA free in the cytoplasm. It may also have one or more **plasmids**. A plasmid is a small ring of DNA, separate from the main loop. Some bacteria also have a **flagellum**, a tail-like structure that makes the cell move.
Sub-cellular structures are the parts inside a cell. Each is adapted to do one job. The table lists the ones you need to know.

rows: Contains the DNA and controls the activities of the cell
Controls which substances enter and leave the cell
Where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy
Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis
Plant cells only (not all of them)
Supports and strengthens the cell. In plants it is made of cellulose
Filled with cell sap. Helps keep the cell firm

blocks.text: The cell wall of a bacterium is not made of cellulose. Bacterial ribosomes are smaller than the ribosomes in eukaryotic cells. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are found only in eukaryotic cells.

diagram.alt: A table comparing animal, plant and bacterial cells. Animal and plant cells are eukaryotic with a nucleus and mitochondria. Plant cells also have chloroplasts, a cellulose cell wall and a permanent vacuole. Bacterial cells are prokaryotic, much smaller, with a loop of DNA, plasmids and a cell wall that is not cellulose.

blocks.text: Cells are too small to measure in metres, so we use prefixes. A **prefix** is a word-start that changes the size of a unit. Each prefix has a matching power of ten, written in **standard form**.
To change millimetres to micrometres, multiply by 1000. To go the other way, divide by 1000. So 0.07 mm is 70 µm.

An **order of magnitude** is a power of ten. To compare two sizes, work out how many times bigger one is and round to the nearest power of ten. A plant cell of 100 µm is 100 times bigger than a bacterial cell of 1 µm. That is 10² times, or two orders of magnitude.

checks.q: Describe where the genetic material is found in a bacterial cell.
checks.a: The DNA is not in a nucleus. It is a single loop free in the cytoplasm, and there may also be plasmids (small rings of DNA).

checks.q: Give the function of the mitochondria.
checks.a: They are where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy.

checks.q: A bacterial cell is 0.002 mm long. Write its length in micrometres and in metres using standard form.
checks.a: 0.002 mm × 1000 = 2 µm. In metres it is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.

exam_phrases: bacterial cell is smaller
does not have its DNA / genetic material inside a nucleus
DNA / genetic material is free in the cytoplasm
has a single loop of DNA
has plasmids (small rings of DNA)
does not have mitochondria
does not have membrane-bound organelles
cell wall is not made of cellulose

mistakes.wrong: Bacterial cells do not have ribosomes.
mistakes.right: Bacterial cells do have ribosomes. They are smaller than the ribosomes in plant and animal cells. This idea is not accepted.

mistakes.wrong: A eukaryotic cell does not have a cell wall.
mistakes.right: Plant cells are eukaryotic and have a cell wall. Say that a bacterial cell has a cell wall that is not made of cellulose, or that animal cells have none.

mistakes.wrong: Mutations in a bacterial cell happen in the nucleus.
mistakes.right: A bacterial cell has no nucleus. Mutations happen in the plasmid, the chromosome or the DNA.

mistakes.wrong: Viruses are not cells because they do not have a cell wall.
mistakes.right: This is not accepted. Say they do not have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, a nucleus, mitochondria or ribosomes.

worked_example.question: Describe four differences between a bacterial cell and a plant cell.
answer_points: The bacterial cell is smaller than the plant cell.
The bacterial cell does not have its DNA inside a nucleus. The plant cell does.
The bacterial cell may have plasmids. The plant cell does not.
The bacterial cell does not have chloroplasts or mitochondria. The plant cell has both.
The cell wall in a bacterial cell is not made of cellulose. The plant cell wall is.
The bacterial cell does not have a large permanent vacuole. The plant cell does.
worked_example.tip: Any four of these score one mark each. Name both cells so the difference is clear.

exam_phrases: no nucleus / chromosomal DNA in the cytoplasm
no membrane-bound organelles
circular / plasmid DNA
flagellum allows movement
cell wall not made of cellulose
mitochondria release energy / aerobic respiration
ribosomes are where proteins are made / protein synthesis
chloroplasts for photosynthesis

mistakes.right: Mitochondria release energy. They are where aerobic respiration happens. "Make" or "produce" energy is ignored.

mistakes.wrong: A bacterial cell has a nucleus and mitochondria.
mistakes.right: A bacterial cell has neither. Its DNA is free in the cytoplasm and it has no membrane-bound organelles.

mistakes.wrong: A bacterial cell has a cell membrane and cytoplasm.
mistakes.right: Plant and animal cells have these too, so they do not score as extra features. Give features such as chromosomal DNA, a cell wall, a flagellum or ribosomes.

mistakes.wrong: Ribosomes make energy for the cell.
mistakes.right: Ribosomes are where proteins are made. Protein synthesis is the word to use.

worked_example.question: Bacterial cells contain plasmids. Describe three other features of a bacterial cell.
answer_points: It has no nucleus. The chromosomal DNA is in the cytoplasm.
It has no membrane-bound organelles, so no mitochondria.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. A slime capsule or pili would also be credited. Cell membrane and cytoplasm are ignored.

exam_phrases: in eukaryotes it is contained in the nucleus
in prokaryotes it is in the cytoplasm
a loop / circle / ring in prokaryotes
prokaryotes have plasmids
ribosome / cell membrane / cytoplasm in both
chloroplast contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis
mitochondria contain enzymes for respiration
cell membrane has receptor molecules for communication

mistakes.wrong: Both types of cell have DNA, so DNA is a similarity between plant and bacterial cells.
mistakes.right: When asked for a similarity in structures, DNA is ignored. Give the cell membrane, cell wall, ribosomes or cytoplasm.

mistakes.wrong: Eukaryotic DNA is a double helix in chromosomes, bacterial DNA is a plasmid.
mistakes.right: These are ignored. Write that eukaryotic DNA is in the nucleus as a linear strand and bacterial DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm.
Mitochondria are in animal cells only. Bacterial cells have no nucleus and no mitochondria, but they do have plasmids.

worked_example.question: Compare the DNA found in eukaryotic and in prokaryotic cells.
answer_points: In eukaryotes the DNA is contained in the nucleus.
In prokaryotes the DNA is in the cytoplasm.
In eukaryotes the DNA is a strand, but in prokaryotes it is a loop.
Prokaryotes have plasmids and eukaryotes do not.
In both, the DNA is made of the same parts: bases, sugar and phosphate.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Compare means both cells appear in each point.
